pr.title: Remove all ConstPropNonsense
pr.description:
We track all locals and projections on them ourselves within the const propagator and only use the InterpCx to actually do some low level operations or read from constants (via `OpTy` we get for said constants).

This helps moving the const prop lint out from the normal pipeline and running it just based on borrowck information. This in turn allows us to make progress on https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/108730#issuecomment-1875557745

there are various follow up cleanups that can be done after this PR (e.g. not matching on Rvalue twice and doing binop checks twice), but lets try landing this one first.

r? @RalfJung
pr.author: oli-obk

processing.reason: The only triggering input for this PR's DataflowConstProp change is a `TrackElem::Variant` projection selecting a variant whose layout ABI is uninhabited. In the historical original, `project_downcast` returned `InvalidProgramInfo::ConstPropNonsense`, so `.ok()` in DataflowConstProp produced `None` and tracking stopped. In the historically incorrect intermediate code, `project_downcast` instead executes `assert!(!layout.abi.is_uninhabited())`; therefore the transformed path aborts with an assertion/ICE before it can produce any return value. On inhabited variants the removed guard makes no difference, and on uninhabited variants the transformed execution is not a defined value-producing execution. Consequently there is no source-grounded pair where both original and transformed functions pass Miri and yield different concrete values. Modeling the assertion as a catchable panic/sentinel or as an unchecked projection returning a value would manufacture semantics not present in the actual historical transformation.

analysis.summary: Cross-pass invariant after ConstPropLint's self-tracking refactor: removing the interpreter's `ConstPropNonsense` rejection makes `project_downcast` assert on uninhabited variants, so DataflowConstProp must check `for_variant(...).abi.is_uninhabited()` and return None before projecting.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the refactor, `InterpCx::project_downcast` checked whether the selected variant layout was uninhabited and returned `throw_inval!(ConstPropNonsense)`. DataflowConstProp's `TrackElem::Variant(idx) => self.ecx.project_downcast(op, idx).ok()` therefore converted that condition into `None` and stopped tracking. ConstPropLint also relied on the interpreter's ConstPropNonsense checks because it stored all locals/places in the interpreter; the PR description says: "We track all locals and projections on them ourselves within the const propagator and only use the InterpCx to actually do some low level operations or read from constants".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Removing ConstPropNonsense and replacing the uninhabited-variant rejection in `project_downcast` with `assert!(!layout.abi.is_uninhabited())`, while leaving DataflowConstProp's variant arm as the unguarded `project_downcast(op, idx).ok()`. The assertion aborts before `.ok()` can recover, so an uninhabited variant that used to be skipped now ICEs.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR constants/enums where the projected variant is uninhabited, as seen by DataflowConstProp variant tracking. Ordinary inhabited variants, plain fields, and scalar projections are outside this trigger. Also applies to any caller of `project_downcast` that can select an uninhabited variant.
analysis.trigger: DataflowConstProp follows a `TrackElem::Variant(idx)` projection into an enum variant whose layout ABI is uninhabited (e.g., a variant containing `!` or an uninhabited field type), after the interpreter-side ConstPropNonsense error was removed.
preconditions: The analyzed MIR contains an enum type with a selected uninhabited variant.
DataflowConstProp is tracking a projection sequence that includes TrackElem::Variant for that variant.
InterpCx::project_downcast now contains `assert!(!layout.abi.is_uninhabited())` instead of returning `InvalidProgramInfo::ConstPropNonsense`.
The old `.ok()` on project_downcast is retained without an uninhabited-variant check.
pitfalls: Only uninhabited variants need the guard; do not skip all variant projections or all field projections.
ConstPropNonsense was an internal invalid-program signal, not a user-facing diagnostic; removing its diagnostic arm is fine only if no caller still relies on the error.
ConstPropLint now tracks its own locals and projections, so it no longer needs interpreter local liveness; do not reintroduce interpreter-state assumptions there.
The guard belongs before `project_downcast`; relying on `.ok()` is insufficient once the error became an assertion.
analysis.testStrategy: Build two programs differing only in the selected enum variant: one selects an inhabited variant with a normal field, the other selects a variant whose type is uninhabited (e.g., `enum E { A(i32), B(i32, !) }` or a field of an empty enum). Run DataflowConstProp on a place projection that includes `Variant(B)` and assert the pass returns no tracked value rather than panicking/ICE; the inhabited variant should still be tracked. Also assert `for_variant(...).abi.is_uninhabited()` is consulted before `project_downcast`.
evidence:
-    /// We are runnning into a nonsense situation due to ConstProp violating our invariants.
-    ConstPropNonsense,

We track all locals and projections on them ourselves within the const propagator and only use the InterpCx to actually do some low level operations or read from constants (via `OpTy` we get for said constants).
